repos.name: Media Clean-Up
repos.summary: A working folder of scripts and logs for consolidating Phil's scattered photos, videos and documents into one correctly dated library, pushing it to iCloud Photos and preparing music, films and TV for a home Plex server, without ever losing an original. It stopped part-way through the iCloud upload.
repos.stack: Python scripts (hashing, perceptual matching, ffprobe, a local Flask swipe-review app with SQLite), PowerShell for reorganising and upload waves, exiftool, icloudpd
notes: Not a git repository. Last activity is 27 Jul 2026, taken from session_log.md and file dates.
Size: about 1.3 GB, of which 82 scripts are the code; the rest is caches, CSV and JSONL manifests, logs and a 41 MB review database. The manifests list personal file paths.

Where it stopped: library organised and backed up locally, music-production folder reorganised and its source deleted, then the iCloud Photos upload stalled on 27 Jul with server-side upload errors and Live Photo pairing problems. The upload orchestrator is stopped and several questions to Phil are unanswered.
The latest state exists only in session_log.md (8,800 lines). DECISIONS.md ends on 23 Jul and CONTEXT.md still describes the plan as of 16 Jul.
Everything refers to the old PC: P:\Projects\mediaCleanUp, a different Windows user folder, and drives E:, I:, D:, F: and G:. Nothing here can run on the new PC without those drives.

Hard safety rule from CONTEXT.md: nothing is deleted until the organised library exists in two places and has been eyeballed. The _ToDelete bin (about 4,600 files, 34 GB) has no backup at all and must wait for a verified iCloud upload.
Several scripts and logs deal with credentials found inside old documents (scan, pull and secure-delete). None of those files, nor any data file, was opened.
A stray file named 'P:ProjectsmediaCleanUprun.log' in the folder is the result of a mistyped path.

items.title: Check the iCloud storage quota to explain the upload failures
items.detail: Uploads fail at Apple's storage service with a repeated put error that fits either a full quota or throttling. Only Phil can read the number from an Apple device or icloud.com; it is the fork in the road for everything else.

items.title: Answer the open questions about the stray ExifTool notification
items.detail: A Windows notification suggested ExifTool was syncing with iCloud Photos. Local checks were negative; still owed: check icloud.com for non-media files, the notification's source app, and whether iCloud Drive sync is configured.

items.title: Decide whether to restart the iCloud Photos client to unjam its file watcher
items.detail: Twelve freshly copied test files were never scanned. A restart may clear the backlog but risks re-sending partial uploads. The last log entry says nothing proceeds until Phil confirms.

items.title: Verify that upload waves 1 to 3 actually reached iCloud
items.detail: About 3,200 files were copied into the sync folder, but none had been confirmed uploaded after 15 hours. The Live Photo markers were stripped from about 680 stills so they upload as plain photos.

items.title: Resume upload waves 4 to 21
items.detail: Eighteen regenerated, pairing-aware waves remain: 8,789 files, about 198 GB. Do not restart the orchestrator until the quota and test batch are settled.

items.title: Verify the iCloud library, then delete _ToDelete and tear down staging (Stage G)
items.detail: Only after the upload is verified on the phone: delete the _ToDelete bin, remove the staging copy and finally the old originals. The bin has no backup, so the order matters.

items.title: Push Documents and Documents_Organized to iCloud Drive
items.detail: These go to iCloud Drive rather than iCloud Photos and are not part of the upload waves.

items.title: Decide what happens to the _Unsure and _ToListen_Screenshots bins
items.detail: 244 files (18 GB) and 190 files respectively, held until Stage G is verified.

items.title: Deep-review E:\Documents
items.detail: 3,230 files parked at Phil's call: about 253 real documents among synth skin images, lesson graphics and junk. Dates and structure need a manual pass.

items.title: Recover dates for about 226 videos with untrustworthy metadata
items.detail: Videos from the 2015 folders and the unknown bin whose embedded dates cannot be trusted; use trip context and the matches now recorded beside dated photos.

items.title: Stage F: tag the music library with MusicBrainz Picard
items.detail: Fix tags, embed art and arrange folders by artist and album. Local only, never to the cloud.

items.title: Stage F: rename films and TV to Plex naming and set up the Plex server
items.detail: Plex naming scheme, let Plex scrape metadata; home server with remote access for Phil only.

items.title: Check the missing _SecretsCheck folder
items.detail: The folder was reported absent on disk and one image pulled out on 19 Jul is not at its recorded path. A separate check is owed.

items.title: Run chkdsk on E: to clear the exFAT dirty flag
items.detail: Flagged at the end of the production clean-up session as something to do when convenient.

items.title: Bring CONTEXT.md and DECISIONS.md up to date with 24 to 27 July
items.detail: Staging to D:, the production reorganisation and deletion, and the whole upload attempt are recorded only in the session log. A cold-start reader of DECISIONS.md would get a state that is four days out of date.

items.title: Put the scripts under version control, apart from data and logs
items.detail: 82 scripts sit loose among manifests, caches and databases with no git history, and several have hand-made .bak copies beside them.

left_out.what: session_log.md was read only for its last entries and DECISIONS.md for its headings and final snapshot; earlier entries may hold small open points that were not picked up.
